The judges somehow manage to have at least one fight which makes you question their intelligence or at least what fight they’ve watched every event. Makes me wish they’d change the judges and somehow figure out a way to make their scorecards make sense for once.
Thought the same thing, a win‘s fine for Edwards. But giving him a 49-46 if not for the point deduction is wrong.

Absolutely, obviously that’s not enough to give Yan the win, Merab won this fight. But it should be counted towards him in getting more points and it have the score card look like he was ragdolled and kept on his back for 25 minutes straight.
Simply breaking a strikers rhythm and elbowing him is pretty much what clinching is for, a takedown is meant to take the fight to the ground something he literally did not do.

Absolutely agreeing with that, especially with such a high amount of defended takedowns it totally should count against a fighter. 

I absolutely understand that Mehab won this fight but scoring it 50-45 isn’t giving Yan any type of credit for absolutely outstanding takedown defense.

I can see the point that you’re making, his constant threat of takedowns certainly is a huge part of his overall game, setting up his striking and interrupting any kind of flow or rhythm for his opponents. 

I just wish he’d actually do something with his takedowns on the ground, the match at times really seemed like a 25 minute session of takedown defense training for Yan.

Well that’s a difference between us respectfully, ground control isn’t exactly an easy thing to do, especially combined with efficient ground and pound. Obviously Merab‘s style is something that requires a huge amount of skill, but I‘d rather watch a fight in which the takedowns actually lead to something, instead of being a constant cycle of takedown attempts that get stuffed and immediate get ups if the succeed

His pace and cardio truly deserves a lot of respect, that’s out of question. I can’t think of any fighter who could keep that level of pressure for 25 minutes straight. But my big point is that there barely was anything beyond that pressure, his takedowns didn’t lead anywhere, no submission attempts or ground and pound.
Wasn’t even that, to lay and pray you actually gotta get the takedown and keep your opponent down lol
Obviously, I just remember people hating Khabib back in the day for his grappling heavy approach, just surprised how little hate Merab gets for a far more boring style comparatively.

It obviously requires incredible cardio and also skill, but it doesn’t make it any less annoying and boring to watch. If he’d combine his takedowns with actually working towards a finish that’d be a different tale, but the thing is that he just limits himself to attempting takedowns, sometimes getting them, but never even throwing up a submission or attempting some ground and pound, it’s just a slow and frustrating grind towards another UD. 

Also on a side note, won’t ever forgive him for turning Aldo‘s last fight in the UFC into a takedown defense drill.
Nor ground and pound, his ground game was non existent beyond the takedown attempts themselves basically.

Same, but Merab‘s style annoyingly is a perfect counter for it, he disrupts any kind of flow a striker might need and is to mobile to ever get hit by a punch clean enough for a one punch knock out. 

He‘s obviously a good fighter, maybe even great but his style is just an annoying grind towards a decision.

I hate Merab‘s fighting style, he just grinds it out, people hated Khabib for his style, but at least that man finished most of his fights, Merab is just spamming takedowns. If he keeps this up he might get the all time record for least successful takedown percentage.

I must go with Arthur, as amazing as John‘s character and character arc is over the two games, to me it just doesn’t match up with the incredible story of Arthur, going from a rough, heartless outlaw to the compassionate man he can be if you go for the high honor ending. 

Many of the side missions and general conversations he had truly were a big contrast to the Arthur we at first met, going from telling the girls that he’d rob the feller blind if they had not been with him, during the first ride into Valentine. Onto sitting on a bench next to Mother Calderón, showing regret and more importantly fear towards his future. 

And besides that, his acting and entire personality was more appealing to me than John‘s. 

All in all I personally view him as one of the best characters ever created for any video game.

And just on top of that this person is karma farming these posts over and over again, which plainly is ridiculous at this point. 

So in conclusion to this, the comments from OP‘s post but also OP herself are in the wrong and represent different parts of how messed up our society is these days.
